claim.label: A centrally led swarm of language-model agents produced more verified-dataset test plans than one agent on the same 20 claims, with zero fabricated identifiers, in two pre-registered experiments (19 vs 13, then 18 vs 12).

evidence.label: Verified-dataset counts, fabricated-identifier counts and costs of the four arms in two pre-registered experiments (centralized 19 and 18 vs single 13 and 12 of 20).

claim.label: Where the single agent fell short of 20 verified datasets, it was mostly because it left plans blank rather than because it named datasets that failed verification (8 of 8 shortfalls blank in experiment 2; 3 blank and 4 named-but-unverified of 7 in experiment 1).

evidence.label: Per-claim triage of the single agent's shortfall: 8 blank of 8 in experiment 2; 3 blank and 4 named-but-unverified of 7 in experiment 1.

claim.label: The led swarm's advantage over the single agent is spread over several distinct claims, not one repeated item: 6 claims in experiment 1 and 7 in experiment 2 were verified by the centralized swarm and not by the single agent, against 0 and 1 the other way.

evidence.label: Per-claim wins of the centralized swarm over the single agent: 6 vs 0 distinct claims in experiment 1, 7 vs 1 in experiment 2.

claim.label: The published "Project Delphi claim" and "Project Delphi evidence item" templates (2026-10-23) state their statements with legacy probknow (pk:) IRIs, while the delphi skill requires Delphi ontology v2.0 terms and says probknow IRIs are never used in new records, so a record written to the skill fails template conformance.

evidence.label: The two served Project Delphi templates (claim, evidence item; 2026-10-23) use pk: terms 11 and 13 times and delphi: terms 0 times; the delphi skill forbids probknow IRIs in new records.

concept.label: Four-arm comparison harness for agent swarms: pre-registered task, mechanical verifier, hard cost cap
